items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: Well, Eckerhardt, Lewis Eckerhardt... he was a very good musician... they kept him on second... I played that season here... during that season in St. Louis... they were still dicking on time to get a fellow

ctx.x: And another, the trumpet you say was a, never could take a hot chorus?

Well, Eckerhardt, Lewis Eckerhardt, that's what it was, yeah. He seemingly was a fellow just out of, youngster just out of school and everything, but he was a very good musician, he could read anything, but his lips didn't allow him to go too high, and they kept him on second, you see, and they tried a couple of times to put him on lead, but he just didn't have the punch to play a solo, or even take a hot solo, you see. At that particular time, but he eventually learned later on. So as I say, I worked on a boat…
Well, to interrupt you again, would the Stratford Spiders musicians or anything? Oh yes, yes.
